clusters.headline_hint: Spain high-speed train collision kills dozens as probe into safety system failures begins

claims.text: A high-speed Renfe train and a stationary Iryo train collided near Urda in central Spain on Wednesday morning.
The train collision near Urda killed 69 people and injured more than 100 people.
Bodies of the crash victims were taken to the main forensics institute in Toledo, where families provided DNA samples for identification.
Julieta Gallego, a 24-year-old Spanish long jumper for Madrid athletics club AD Sprint, died in the crash.
Former Spanish employment minister Fátima Báñez, 59, who chaired the Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations (CEOE), was killed in the crash.
Fátima Báñez served in the Spanish government under former Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy from 2011 until 2018 as Spain's first female employment minister.
Civil Guard officer José Manuel Chacón, 31, and finance lawyer Antonio Montero Domínguez were among those killed in the crash.
Spain began three days of official mourning on Thursday following the deadly train collision.
Spanish train drivers went on strike to demand increased investment in railway safety.
Spain's foreign ministry reported that 42 foreign citizens from seven countries were involved in the crash, leaving one dead and at least seven injured.
Spanish Transport Minister Óscar Puente described rear-end collisions as highly unlikely and suggested human error under inexplicable circumstances caused the crash.
The Guardia Civil established offices in Madrid, Toledo, Córdoba, and Seville to collect DNA samples from relatives of missing victims.
The Guardia Civil reported that 64 people had been reported missing by relatives by Thursday morning.
A computer malfunction at 8:30am on Wednesday disabled the LZB train control system across a 69-km stretch of track.
Operators at Madrid's Atocha station control centre allegedly instructed the AVE train driver to resume at normal speed despite the signalling system failure.
The Renfe AVE train struck the stationary Iryo train from behind at approximately 8:53am near Urda.
Railway safety procedures require trains to travel at a sight speed of no more than 40 kmph under trackside signalling when the LZB system is offline.
The AVE train travelled approximately 25 km after resuming its journey before colliding with the stationary Iryo train.
Spain's high-speed rail network carried 45 million passengers last year.
Vox leader Santiago Abascal accused the Spanish government of being a criminal organization following the collision.

clusters.headline_hint: ECB President Christine Lagarde resigns early to speak out on global affairs

claims.text: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde announced she will step down early from her position.
Christine Lagarde will officially leave her post as ECB President on February 7, 2027, nine months before the scheduled end of her eight-year term.
Christine Lagarde took office in October 2019 as the first ECB president without formal economics training or prior central banking experience.
French President Emmanuel Macron thanked Christine Lagarde for her determined leadership at the head of the ECB through numerous crises.
Lagarde announced her early resignation at the conclusion of a press conference where the ECB decided to hold its key deposit rate at 2.5%.
Eurozone inflation rose to 3.8% last month, reaching its highest point since September 2023.
Christine Lagarde stated she was stepping down because she wanted freedom of speech and expression to engage on matters outside monetary policy.
European Council President António Costa announced that the appointment process for Lagarde's successor would begin immediately.
French government bond yields climbed to their highest level in 25 years during a political standoff over next year's budget.

clusters.headline_hint: Israeli election ends in deadlock as Netanyahu falls short of majority amid accusations against Arab parties

claims.text: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed Arab Israeli parties used foreign funding to steal Tuesday's election after his coalition lost its majority.
Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies requested Shin Bet to investigate alleged vote-buying in Palestinian communities in Israel.
Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot accused Likud and Netanyahu of running an organized campaign to delegitimize the election results.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged political leaders to avoid tarnishing an entire community exercising its right to vote.
Qatari government adviser Majed al-Ansari categorically denied claims that Qatar provided funding to influence Israeli elections.
Final vote tallies placed Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition at 53 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc at 48 seats in the 120-member Knesset.
The Arab party lists Joint List and Ra'am secured a combined 19 seats in the election.
Securing a governing majority in the Israeli Knesset requires a coalition of at least 61 seats.
Central Elections Committee head Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg asked Shin Bet to investigate allegations of foreign interference.
Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh called Likud's fraud accusations a racist blood libel designed to overturn election results.
Arab Israelis make up approximately one-fifth of Israel's population.
Likud emerged as the single largest party in the Knesset, securing 27 seats.

clusters.headline_hint: Pentagon fires top army general Brett Sylvia over leaks of classified information

claims.text: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, head of the Joint Chiefs of Staff's J5 directorate, over alleged leaks of classified information.
An internal investigation report stated Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia admitted to sharing classified details about the wars in Iran and Ukraine with two journalists.
Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia failed multiple polygraph tests during the Pentagon's leak investigation.
The internal report noted Sylvia met a journalist in person at a Silver Diner in Arlington, Virginia, to orally share details about US military assistance to Ukraine.
President Donald Trump stated that Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia had big problems and affirmed the administration was actively searching for leakers.
Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell confirmed personnel action was taken against an individual following an Air Force OSI investigation.
The Pentagon referred Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia's leak case to the US Department of Justice for criminal investigation.
In July 2026, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a joint Pentagon-DOJ task force to identify and prosecute unauthorized disclosures to the press.
A Department of Defense official clarified that Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia was not a central planner for the Iran war, which is directed by CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper.
Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia previously commanded the 101st Airborne Division at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, until May 2025.

clusters.headline_hint: Russian drone strike on Dnipro railway station kills 14 in Ukraine

claims.text: A Russian drone strike killed at least 14 people at the main railway station in Dnipro, Ukraine.
The drone strike at Dnipro railway station injured at least 14 people, including an 11-year-old boy.
Ukrainian railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia stated a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was at the platform when the drone struck.
A Russian missile strike on Chernihiv killed two 15-year-old girls and injured 25 people.
A Russian drone attack in Kremenchuk killed three people and injured 28 after hitting residential buildings and a school.
Local authorities declared Friday a day of mourning in Chernihiv and Dnipro.
The mayor of Moscow stated 613 Ukrainian drones were launched towards the Moscow region overnight.
Ukrzaliznytsia reported that nearly 60% of the 521 locomotives damaged since February 2022 were hit during 2026.
Ukrainian defense firm The Fourth Law manufactures the Lupynis-10-TFL-1 autonomous drone, which utilizes onboard AI terminal guidance during the final 500 meters of flight.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that artificial intelligence could make autonomous decisions on the battlefield as early as next year.

clusters.headline_hint: Supreme Court directs banks to compensate victims of digital arrest scams

claims.text: The Supreme Court instructed the Reserve Bank of India that its proposed standard operating procedure must require banks to compensate account holders who lose savings to digital arrest scams.
A Supreme Court bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the Reserve Bank of India to submit a list of authorised banks and financial institutions.
Amicus curiae V S Nappinai urged the Supreme Court to extend financial liability for digital arrest scams to telecom service providers.
The Supreme Court asked WhatsApp whether features could be developed to automatically disconnect unusually long calls or provide a kill switch against fraudsters.
Attorney General R. Venkataramani told the Supreme Court that digital arrest cases decreased by approximately 50% compared to the previous year.
The Supreme Court granted the Reserve Bank of India time until November 30 to submit the proposed Know Your Customer Amendment Directions, 2026.

A report by the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre and Ministry of Home Affairs stated that over 21,900 digital arrest fraud complaints involving more than Rs 647 crore were registered in the first eight months of 2026.
In August, the Supreme Court instructed the Reserve Bank of India to establish a standard operating procedure for banks to handle cyber-enabled financial fraud and mule accounts.
Chief Justice Surya Kant questioned why victims continue to fall for digital arrest scams despite media coverage, asking, 'What is wrong with victims? Are they not normal persons?'
Delhi police arrested two men in October 2026 for operating a mule account used to process money from a Rs 2.10-crore digital arrest scam.
In Kozhikode, a 57-year-old woman lost Rs 1.35 crore after scammers impersonating Mumbai Crime Branch officers ordered her to transfer money to the Reserve Bank of India for verification.
Digital arrest fraudsters typically pose as law enforcement officers on video calls made from setups designed to look like government offices or police stations.

clusters.headline_hint: Cyclone Arnab damages Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, marooning hundreds of villages

claims.text: Cyclone Arnab weakened into a depression over central Chhattisgarh on October 29, 2026.
Andhra Pradesh Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar estimated that Cyclone Arnab caused at least Rs 500 crore in damage to the state's electricity infrastructure.
Andhra Pradesh health officials relocated 3,100 pregnant women to medical facilities prior to Cyclone Arnab, resulting in 367 births at the hospitals.
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu stated that Cyclone Arnab caused a preliminary estimated loss of Rs 4,600 crore to the state.
The Odisha state government planned to airlift 120 people stranded by heavy rains and flooding in Ganjam district.
Patrapur in Ganjam district recorded 546 mm of rain in 24 hours ending at 8:30 am on Thursday, marking Odisha's highest single-day rainfall at a single location in 35 years.
Floodwaters completely washed away a 300-metre section of National Highway 326 at Ledabandha in Gajapati district.
Railways canceled nine trains and diverted 14 others after floodwaters exceeded safety levels on bridges in the Ichchapuram-Jhadupudi section.
A new low-pressure area formed over the south Andaman Sea at 5:30 a.m. on October 29, 2026.
Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu stated that seven people died in Andhra Pradesh as a result of Cyclone Arnab.
Andhra Pradesh announced compensation of Rs 1,500 for each fallen coconut and oil palm tree destroyed during Cyclone Arnab.
Andhra Pradesh Municipal Administration Minister P. Narayana stated that 85 locations across 10 municipalities in eight districts were damaged by Cyclone Arnab.

clusters.headline_hint: Supreme Court rebukes Corporate Affairs Ministry over interference in NCLT appointments

claims.text: Chief Justice Surya Kant remarked that the National Company Law Tribunal and National Company Law Appellate Tribunal have been 'completely hijacked' by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
Senior advocate Sanjiv Sen told the Supreme Court that 253 out of 320 regular posts in the National Company Law Tribunal remain vacant.
Senior advocate Meenakshi Arora stated that the Ministry of Corporate Affairs outsourced the recruitment of NCLT contractual employees to a foreign firm.
Chief Justice Surya Kant directed that recruitment for tribunal staff should be handled through the UPSC or Staff Selection Commission rather than contractual outsourcing.
The Supreme Court ordered the presidents of the NCLT and NCLAT to submit detailed proposals on infrastructure, building, and staffing needs within four weeks.
The court was informed that two floors at the NCLT Principal Bench building had to be shut down due to collapsing infrastructure.
The NCLT Bar Association stated that 18 NCLT benches were operating half-day sittings due to shortages of judicial and technical members.
An Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India report noted that ongoing corporate insolvency resolution processes averaged 713 days as of March 2025, exceeding the 270-day statutory limit.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 noted that nearly 30,600 cases were pending before the NCLT as of March 2025.

clusters.headline_hint: Piyush Goyal asserts India-US trade deal will safeguard domestic farmers

claims.text: Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and the United States reached approximately $240 billion in 2025.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Mumbai and Jamnagar during a trip to India.
The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 authorised tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas.
Union Minister Piyush Goyal stated that the India-US trade agreement will fully protect the sensitive interests of domestic farmers.
India withdrew from negotiations for the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) on November 4, 2019, in Bangkok.
Union Minister Piyush Goyal stated that 60% of India's installed electricity capacity is derived from green and renewable sources.
Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that the Modi government has concluded eight free trade agreements.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated that the India-US trade deal negotiations are in their 'last mile'.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated regarding the trade agreement with India, 'I would say we're about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement.'
